analysis.title: The State of Nuclear Power and Small Modular Reactors (October 22, 2026 update)
key_insights: Nuclear equities sold off despite new contracts: Needham's nuclear-reactor group fell 19.2% in the week to October 16, Oklo fell 19.4% to $27.97, Centrus 19.3% to $114.94, NANO Nuclear 16.0% to $12.88. Needham reads it as a repricing of financing and execution risk, not power demand.

Needham says data-center construction is now underwritten above $13m per megawatt before GPUs, and Cipher's Barber Lake budget of about $2.95bn (roughly $14m/MW) came with an unexpected $850m convertible. A recovery needs project financings to close at attractive loan-to-cost ratios, stable budgets and higher lease income per megawatt.

Constellation fell 13.6% from $299.59 on October 8 to $258.84 on October 20, 26.4% lower for the year. J.P. Morgan's desk saw supply from investors reducing exposure after the contract wins. IPPs fell 3.5% in the week to October 20 against +0.3% for utilities.
2026 around-the-clock power at PJM West fell 7.4% in a week to $62.75/MWh and 2027 fell 4.3% to $70.38. NI Hub 2026 fell 2.8% to $36.58.

SpaceX's October 20 third-quarter call, as J.P. Morgan reports it, cited a 'blue sky' case of 20 GW of additional power and cooling next year with high confidence in at least 10 GW, and lifted the power complex the next day.

Scotiabank cut IPP targets 18-31% on September 29, admitted it incorrectly expected a news-flow drought until after the midterms, notes rising short interest in Constellation, Vistra and Talen, and calls FERC's five-month delay to PJM's backstop a material negative. It is 'more bearish than most on PJM'. Yuanta takes the opposite side, calling the Google contract the first bring-your-own-power template for PJM.

HSBC notes the utility sector has de-rated to about 16x forward earnings on rising Treasury yields. The contracts lift earnings mostly after 2029, while the forward curve and discount rate moved against holders.

CIBC initiates Constellation at Outperformer, $358 target (equal weight of 13.5x 2028 EV/EBITDA and 5.75% FCF yield), with adjusted EBITDA rising from $4.6bn in 2025 to $11.0bn in 2028 and 2028 adjusted EPS of $16.95. Balance-sheet flexibility is the main argument: FFO at about 30% of net debt in 2027 versus an 18% peer average, leverage 2.2x versus 3.5x.

HSBC initiates Constellation at Buy, $335 (15.6x 2027 EBITDA of $8.87bn). It sees three layers of nuclear price support (45U floor near $45/MWh, PJM capacity uplift of $14-15/MWh, 15-20 year contracts near $75/MWh or more) and models an implied nuclear price in the mid-$80s by 2029-30, EPS of $23.71 in 2030 and $14bn of buybacks over 2026-30.

Raymond James raises Constellation to $341 from $336 at Outperform on about 22x 2028 EPS of $15.50 and cuts its Q3 estimate to $3.90 from $4.40, still about 8% above the $3.62 consensus. Most of the roughly 1 GW of uprates in the 5 GW PJM Cycle 1 pipeline is committed. Uprates split roughly evenly between NI Hub (low end of the $20-50/MWh premium range) and PJM West (high end).
Scotiabank's crude estimate puts the 3.6 GW Google package at up to about $2 of EPS (roughly 10%), with Sector Outperform and $355 kept while estimates are under review.

The four new Constellation targets average about $347, 34% above the October 20 price but 7% below the six incumbents. Raymond James' target peaked at $406 in February. Houses agree on 2028 EPS of $15.50-16.95, so the spread comes from the multiple.

CIBC initiates Talen at Outperformer, $499 (10.0x 2028 EV/EBITDA, 9.75% FCF yield), the highest Talen target in the series, citing about 41% annual EBITDA growth and 60% FCF per share growth from 2025 to 2028 and the 17-year 1.9 GW AWS contract. The $1.5bn securitization of 2027-29 PJM capacity payments funds a buyback of about 10% of shares.

HSBC rates all four IPPs Buy (Talen $444.30, Vistra $190, NRG $179, Constellation $335). Its Talen case sees limited further clean contracting with 85% of nuclear output contracted to Amazon through 2042, and relies on 1.5 GW of gas uprates by 2032 and $5.5bn of buybacks. Scotiabank rates Talen Sector Perform at $386, its first non-positive rating in the series.
PSEG now has only neutral ratings in the series: HSBC Hold $72.50, J.P. Morgan Neutral $77, Jefferies Hold $69.

HSBC doubles its US data-center consumption forecast to about 900 TWh in 2030 (+80%) and 1,800 TWh in 2035 (+94%). Total load growth is about 2.2 PWh by 2035. It expects only 4-5 GW of nuclear growth against 260 GW of renewables and storage and 180 GW of gas over ten years. BNEF sees 13.7 GW of nuclear additions through 2036 and up to 67.8 GW of new gas by 2030. Neither gives new reactors a material role before the 2030s.

NRC's expected uprate applications total about 2.4 GW (2,421 MW) through 2032 against a 5 GW administration target for 2030. Roughly 1.5 GW has a buyer or federal financing (890 MW Google, 190 MW Calvert Cliffs for Amazon, 433 MW DOE-financed for Vistra). Reaching 5 GW needs another 2.6 GW of applications not yet on the list. Restarts add 2,255 MW (Palisades 805 MW, Crane 835 MW, Duane Arnold 615 MW).

AEP and X-energy signed a joint development agreement for a 960 MW plant of twelve 80 MW Xe-100s at the Breed coal station in Sullivan County, Indiana, with Amazon funding development and intending to buy the output. Construction needs a final investment decision and no cost or schedule was disclosed. J.P. Morgan reads it as delivery on the 1 GW utility agreement it flagged.

UBS keeps X-energy at Buy with a $34 target (cut from $40), shares at $10.36, the bottom of a 52-week range topping at $35.98. Its model takes revenue from $218m this year to $2.16bn in 2030. Seadrift construction permit is expected in early 2027.

AtkinsRéalis signed a memorandum with Indiana and Hoosier Energy to explore up to eight CANDU units and 6 GW. CIBC calls it a modest positive with no near-term backlog since financing, offtake and timelines are undefined. J.P. Morgan sizes the opportunity at about $12-24bn.

The Nuclear Company proposed Prosperity One in Lewis County, Kentucky: up to six AP1000s and 6.6 GW, construction targeted for 2028, with no NRC licence application, financing or offtake disclosed. Deep Fission signed a binding 25-year master energy purchase agreement for about 150 MW in Parsons, Kansas, targeting operation September 30, 2028, but the offtaker has no minimum purchase.

None of the four nuclear announcements discloses a price, capital cost or construction contract. Sites are brownfield or state-designated, gas comes first where possible, and the buyer carries most of the risk.

Barclays downgrades NuScale to Underweight from Equal Weight and cuts the target to $5 from $11 (shares $5.69) because no definitive TVA-ENTRA1 PPA for 6 GW has been announced. It sees negotiations running into 2027, questions ENTRA1's record, and flags liquidity risk: $1.9bn cash at end of Q2, about $139m quarterly operating outflow, a $750m ATM programme and about $3.2bn of further equity assumed through mid-2029. Upside and downside cases are $19 and $1.

Barclays keeps Oklo at Overweight but cuts the target to $59 from $76 on higher capital cost assumptions (about $500m per initial 75 MW Aurora, up from $450m). Cases are $117 and $29. It expects a regulatory lull after the Aurora-INL preliminary safety analysis approval. This is the fourth Oklo target cut in four weeks, after UBS $41, Seaport $71 and Goldman $49. DOE's Launch Pad selected Oklo's Groves-2 Forge for lutetium-177 work, which Needham sees as limited near-term financial effect.

Canaccord keeps Deep Fission at Buy, $18 target against a $2.81 share price, flagging capital as the binding constraint: about $40m expected year-end cash against a $200m pilot programme with $40m spent. It expects the company to need more capital, consistent with Maxim's call for a raise in 1H27.

NANO Nuclear's KRONOS review schedule: draft environmental assessment and safety evaluation in February 2027, final assessment in May, final safety evaluation in September, supporting construction from 2H27. Needham rates it Buy, $33.

Samsung Securities argues the November 3 midterms change the timing, not the direction, of US nuclear policy, since support rests on bipartisan law. At risk are the $17.5bn American Nuclear Supply Chain Loans for up to ten AP1000s (seven undisclosed sites) and NRC reform under Executive Order 14300. The NRC's 3-2 Republican majority is unlikely to shift soon.

Affordability shapes deal structures: Microsoft pays for new generation under a 20-year NiSource agreement (about $1.8bn customer savings per NiSource), and Google expanded its Entergy Arkansas partnership. New York is the only state with a one-year data-center moratorium and a Virginia senator proposed a three-year pause.

Barclays sustainable-investing team reads 2026 as nuclear policy moving from endorsement to enablement, citing phase-out reversals in Switzerland, Italy, Taiwan and Belgium, Korea's 11th Basic Plan, India's SHANTI Act, and a bipartisan fusion bill authorizing about $10bn that is not expected to pass this Congress.

Samsung Securities rates KEPCO E&C Buy with a W160,000 target against J.P. Morgan's Neutral at W130,000. On Doosan Enerbility Samsung's Buy at W112,000 is below J.P. Morgan's W130,000. KEPCO is considering a symbolic-level stake of 5-10% in Westinghouse alongside private Korean firms, with no allocation decided.

Two dated predictions on the TVA-ENTRA1 PPA (Goldman July 17, Truist August 11) are now at risk. J.P. Morgan's August 19 call for an X-energy 1 GW utility deal was delivered as a joint development agreement.

Watch items into November: GE Vernova (Oct 28), Cameco (Oct 30), Centrus (~Nov 4), Oklo (~Nov 10), Constellation and IPPs early November; PJM backstop refiling by Oct 29; midterms Nov 3; Korea-US workshare late October.

sector_views.rationale: Barclays downgrades NuScale and cuts Oklo. Four consecutive Oklo target cuts and widest target-to-price gaps among developers. Neither HSBC nor BNEF gives new reactors a material role before the 2030s.
Houses agree on inputs (uprates, nuclear price, EPS per contracted GW) but differ on how much to pay before 2029. Scotiabank bearish on PJM, HSBC all Buy, CIBC bullish on Talen.
HSBC notes the sector de-rated to about 16x forward earnings on rising yields while fundamentals improved. PSEG ratings all neutral.
About 2.4 GW of expected applications and 2.3 GW of restarts form the realistic near-term nuclear additions, with 1.5 GW already contracted or financed.

earnings_insights: Constellation Q3 2026 EPS: Raymond James estimate $3.90 (cut from $4.40), about 8% above $3.62 consensus est. Not yet reported; due early November.
Constellation 2028 adjusted EPS estimates: CIBC $16.95, HSBC $16.94, Wolfe $16.76, Raymond James $15.50, all estimates. HSBC models 2030 EPS of $23.71 (estimate).

Constellation company sensitivity: $0.40-1.00 of annual EPS per gigawatt of existing output contracted at the premium. Scotiabank estimates up to about $2 of EPS (roughly 10%) from the 3.6 GW Google package (estimate).
Talen 2028 free cash flow per share estimated at $47.43 by CIBC (estimate), with about 41% annual EBITDA growth 2025-2028.
Upcoming reports: GE Vernova (October 28), Cameco (October 30), Centrus (~November 4), Oklo (~November 10), Constellation and IPPs in early November.
X-energy UBS model: revenue $218m this year to $2.16bn in 2030, operating profit turning positive at $229m in 2030 (estimates).
NuScale liquidity: $1.9bn cash at end of Q2 2026 (reported), average operating outflow of about $139m a quarter since start of 2025.
Deep Fission: management expects about $71.7m cash at end of Q3 and about $40m at year-end against a $200m pilot programme of which $40m is spent. Canaccord retains $242.6m of 2029 revenue.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Forwards fell with equities, a headwind for IPP valuations.
Lower forward curve cuts merchant revenue expectations for generators.
Illinois pricing is weaker than PJM West.

macro_indicators.interpretation: HSBC forecast raised +80% and +94% versus its prior view, supporting a long-run demand case for power.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Growth is mostly restarts and uprates, not new reactors.

risk_factors: Cost of capital and AI-infrastructure financing risk, including data-center budgets above $13m per megawatt and surprise convertible issuance.
Rising Treasury yields compressing utility multiples.
PJM backstop delay and possible capacity price weakness if new supply exceeds market assumptions.
TVA-ENTRA1 PPA delays and NuScale liquidity and dilution risk.
Developer funding gaps, notably Deep Fission's cash against its pilot budget.
Midterm-driven delays to the $17.5bn AP1000 loan programme and NRC reform.
Interconnection queues limiting merchant contracting of uprates.
Data-center moratoria and affordability pressure on utility contract structures.
Oklo capital cost inflation and continued target cuts.
vol_and_positioning: Scotiabank records rising short interest in Constellation, Vistra and Talen.
Oklo ended the week 83.7% below its 52-week high, NANO 74.1% and Centrus 72.1%.
Goldman's July 10 call that crowded positioning could reverse hard is described as borne out again by the 19.2% weekly fall in the reactor group.
J.P. Morgan's trading desk saw supply in Constellation from investors reducing exposure after the contract wins.
Wolfe's IPP sentiment meter call (to 4) was tested by the 3.5% IPP drop.
geopolitical: Midterm elections on November 3, with a Democratic House the market's base case and six pivotal Senate races (Alaska, Texas, Michigan, Iowa, Ohio, Maine) within the margin of error.
Korea-US framework: KEPCO considering a 5-10% stake in Westinghouse, with Macquarie expecting a workshare by late October and no Westinghouse IPO filing.
FERC's five-month delay to PJM's backstop procurement, with a PJM refiling expected by October 29.
Switzerland, Italy, Taiwan and Belgium reversing nuclear phase-outs, and India's SHANTI Act opening civil nuclear to private capital.
New York's one-year data-center moratorium and a proposed three-year Virginia pause.
EU Innovation Fund awarded €3.4bn to 77 projects including Calogena's heat-only SMR pilot in France.

tension_points.bull_case: Yuanta argues the Google contract is a bring-your-own-power template and capacity expansion at existing plants revalues every IPP with retrofittable nuclear. HSBC rates all four IPPs Buy on contracting and pricing optionality.
tension_points.bear_case: Scotiabank is more bearish than most on PJM, calls FERC's backstop delay a material negative, expects new supply to weigh on long-term energy and capacity prices, and notes rising short interest.
tension_points.what_invalidates: PJM refiling of the backstop by October 29 and FERC's response within sixty days, plus whether PJM West forwards recover after the 7% weekly drop.

tension_points.bull_case: CIBC says the market still assigns insufficient value to contracting upside and reinvestment. HSBC models an implied nuclear price in the mid-$80s by 2029-30 and EPS of $23.71 in 2030.
tension_points.bear_case: Contracts lift earnings mostly after 2029 while forwards and the discount rate moved against holders. J.P. Morgan's desk saw holders cut exposure after the contract wins.

tension_points.bull_case: CIBC sees the strongest forward growth in the peer group, with about 41% annual EBITDA growth and about 4 GW of land and data-center upside.
tension_points.bear_case: HSBC sees limited scope for further clean contracts with 85% of nuclear output contracted to Amazon through 2042. Scotiabank rates it Sector Perform.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman expected a finalized TVA-ENTRA1 PPA before end-2026 and Truist modelled a binding 1 GWe agreement in 4Q26.

tension_points.what_invalidates: A definitive TVA-ENTRA1 PPA announced before the end of 2026 would invalidate the bear case. Slippage into 2027 would invalidate the Goldman and Truist predictions.
